- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) or shows sharp decline, model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is neutral or mixed; add 1–2% buffer to initial days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often fails to capture mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.0–0.3) over 5+ days, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment improves.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out forecast changes if sentiment shifts by <0.2 in 3 consecutive days.
- In cases where true outcome is significantly lower than forecast (e.g., >5% below), check if sentiment was bullish recently — if so, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If forecast is consistently higher than true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, consider sentiment decay — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
